Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder

Ryan Powell

As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

Daniel Leal/AFP via Getty Images

Nov 20, 2026
5 min read

VIENNA—A healthy information environment depends on supply and demand for quality inputs. To remain competitive and independent in an AI-powered ecosystem, news outlets, publishers, research institutes, and NGOs will need to develop their own skills and tools for establishing where information comes from and whether it can be trusted. Otherwise, they will lose the independence they need to set their agenda in dialogue with audiences and serve the public interest.
